notes: New look: a black-and-white Summit mark (two peaks, one snow line) on the startup screen, in the menu bar, About and the installer

Photo wallpapers: eight real mountain and landscape photographs (Summit, Dolomites, Yosemite, Alpine Lake, Highlands, Desert, Dunes, Coast), each with a day picture for Light and a night picture for Dark. Summit is the new default; the colour wallpapers are still there
Windows open, close and minimise more slowly and settle gently instead of snapping
Launchpad: the icon under the pointer grows and its neighbours follow in a ripple
The same red, yellow and green window buttons in every app, including apps that draw their own title bar, App Store apps, Chrome and Firefox

iCloud (in Launchpad): Mail, Photos, iCloud Drive, Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Contacts, Find My, Pages, Numbers, Keynote, Apple Music and Apple TV in their own windows, signed in with your Apple Account on Apple's page
Summit Drop (in Launchpad): send photos and files to and from an iPhone, iPad or Mac on the same Wi-Fi by scanning a code; nothing to install on the Apple device
Settings → Sharing: a new Apple section with iCloud, Summit Drop, iPhone and iPad by cable (they appear in Files), Macs on this network, and AirPlay Speakers
